style.vernacular: Central European Austro-Hungarian city: Lower Town (Donji grad) street blocks of three- to four-storey plastered tenements in pale yellow, ochre, cream and pink with sash windows, cornices and Secession details under hip roofs of red-brown tile; Upper Town and Kaptol with baroque and neo-Gothic churches; Zagorje and Turopolje villages of white rendered houses and manor castles with red clay-tile roofs; socialist-era exposed-concrete faculties and slab blocks in Novi Zagreb; glass-and-render malls and offices around the ring roads, among linden, chestnut and plane trees.
style.ornament: Secession and historicist stucco ornament, sash and arched windows with moulded surrounds, cornices, wrought-iron balconies, baroque church towers with onion-shaped helmets, neo-Gothic spires, brutalist concrete relief and pilotis, and baroque manor frescoes and pediments.
